name: Introduction to Statistical Data Science
pre_requisite: Mathematics for AI-I (TMA102); Mathematics for AI-II (TMA203)
difficulty_reason: Applied statistics course: probability distributions, random variables, MCMC, covariance, correlation, regression, Bayes/Naive Bayes, CLT, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests (Z, t, chi-square, ANOVA) practised in Excel/Python. Moderate mathematical load; programming is light.
key_background_areas: Mathematics for AI-I and II (probability, linear algebra, calculus); basic Python or Excel
syllabus_topics: Data science components and applications; probability and distributions (Normal, Bernoulli, Binomial, Negative Binomial, Geometric, Poisson); discrete and continuous random variables, Markov-chain Monte Carlo; descriptive statistics, sample covariance, correlation, covariance matrix, outlier detection; correlation, least squares, simple and multiple linear regression; Naive Bayes, Bayesian classification, Central Limit Theorem, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, Z-score; Z-test, t-test, chi-square, one-way ANOVA, p-values
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 3rd-Sem-Syllabus-2025-29-Batch-1.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Python Programming
pre_requisite: Fundamental of Computer & Introduction to Programming (TCS101); Programming for Problem Solving (TCS201)
difficulty_reason: Introductory-to-intermediate Python: syntax, data structures, OOP, then NumPy/Pandas/Matplotlib/Seaborn and basic EDA. No real mathematics; load is hands-on coding that builds on first-year programming.
key_background_areas: Basic programming (TCS101/TCS201); basic logic
syllabus_topics: Python basics, data types, functions and modules, exception handling basics; lists, tuples, dictionaries, text/binary file I/O; OOP (classes, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation); NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn; data cleaning and EDA (summary statistics, correlation, histograms, scatter and box plots)
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/3rd-Semester-Syllabus-July-Dec-2025.pdf

name: Responsible and Explainable AI
difficulty_reason: Mostly conceptual: AI ethics, bias, fairness metrics, transparency, privacy and societal impact, plus XAI methods (LIME, SHAP, feature importance, heatmaps, PDPs) implemented in Python. Light mathematics; limited coding. Syllabus has a template error (Unit 4 is titled 'Searching and Sorting' but its content is XAI).
key_background_areas: Fundamentals of AI and ML; basic Python
syllabus_topics: AI ethics, types of bias (data, algorithmic, interactional), detecting and mitigating bias, fairness metrics and trade-offs; transparency, accountability frameworks, surveillance and privacy, data protection laws; societal impact on employment, governance and policy; XAI fundamentals, LIME, SHAP, feature importance, decision trees and rule-based explanations; heatmaps, partial dependence plots, activation visualizations; XAI in finance, healthcare and autonomous systems
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 3rd-Sem-Syllabus-2025-29-Batch-1.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Fundamental of Cloud Computing and Big Data
difficulty_reason: Descriptive survey of cloud service/deployment models, providers, AWS services and big data terminology. No mathematics and almost no programming (one cloud deployment exercise); main burden is breadth of terminology.
key_background_areas: Basic computer/internet awareness; no formal prerequisite
syllabus_topics: Cloud vision, history, NIST characteristics; cluster vs grid vs cloud; public/private/hybrid/community deployment; IaaS, PaaS, SaaS (EC2, Eucalyptus, OpenStack, Google App Engine, Azure, Salesforce); big data characteristics, techniques and analytics overview; AWS foundation services (Lambda, RDS, S3, CloudFront, Glacier, SNS); SLAs, billing, cloud economics and risks; design and deploy an online video subscription app on the cloud
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/3rd-Semester-Syllabus-July-Dec-2025.pdf

name: Joy of Computing using Python
difficulty_reason: First-course Python programming (NPTEL/SWAYAM, IIT Ropar): prerequisite is only 10th standard. Project-style topics (sorting, searching, ciphers, sentiment analysis, recursion, PageRank) with light probability ideas (birthday paradox, Monty Hall). Easy entry, though breadth of mini-projects is wide.
key_background_areas: No formal prerequisite (high-school level); basic logical thinking
syllabus_topics: Variables and expressions, loops and conditionals, lists and tuples, abstraction/functions; birthday paradox, Monty Hall, sorting, searching, substitution cipher, sentiment analysis, permutations, word counting, recursion (Tower of Hanoi), image processing, tic-tac-toe, Snakes and Ladders, six degrees of separation, PageRank
syllabus_source: https://arctest.dev.nptel.ac.in/content/syllabus_pdf/106106182.pdf (NPTEL, IIT Ropar). Alternative: GEHU publishes no syllabus text for TCS361, but the Jul 2026 GEHU Sem III timetable lists it as 'Joy of Computing using Python - Through Swayam (ONLINE)', an exact title match with this NPTEL course.

name: Statistical Learning for Reliability Analysis
pre_requisite: Engineering Mathematics-I (TMA101) or Mathematics for AI-I (TMA102); Engineering Mathematics-II (TMA201) or Mathematics for AI-II (TMA203); Discrete Structures and Combinatorics (TMA316) or Advanced Probability for AI (TCS368); Python Programming (TCS346) or Introduction to Python Programming (TCS102)
difficulty_reason: Statistics-heavy NPTEL course (IIT Kharagpur): hypothesis testing, paired t-tests, ANOVA, maximum likelihood estimation, non-parametric inference, classification and entropy, all applied to reliability analysis. Assumes prior statistical inference and linear algebra; abstract quantitative load. Weeks 2-4 and 7 not seen.
key_background_areas: Probability and statistics (inference, hypothesis testing, likelihood); linear algebra; calculus; Python (per GEHU prerequisites)
syllabus_topics: Reliability and reliability estimation, concept of statistical learning; parametric statistical inference and case studies; non-parametric inference (correlation, relation, regression analysis); single-population learning and paired t-tests; multi-population learning and ANOVA; maximum likelihood estimation; statistical data classification; entropy in statistical learning
syllabus_source: https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/syllabus_pdf/106105239.pdf and https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc23_cs84/preview (NPTEL, IIT Kharagpur; Alternative: GEHU's own syllabus not seen)

name: Introduction to Cryptography
difficulty_reason: Mix of descriptive security concepts and moderate number-theoretic maths (primes, Euclidean/extended Euclidean algorithm, Euler's totient) with working through ciphers, DES/Feistel, RSA and hashing. Algorithms must be traced or coded but no deep proofs.
key_background_areas: Basic number theory and modular arithmetic; basic programming for implementing algorithms; networking basics
syllabus_topics: OSI security architecture, attacks, services, mechanisms; classical ciphers (substitution, transposition), steganography basics; symmetric encryption, Feistel structure, simple DES, double DES, stream ciphers/RC4, pseudorandom numbers; key distribution; prime numbers, Euclidean and extended Euclidean algorithms, Euler's totient; RSA; message authentication, MD5; intruders, intrusion detection, malware, firewalls; cybercrime, IP, privacy and ethics
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/3rd-Semester-Syllabus-July-Dec-2025.pdf

name: Fundamentals of Statistics and AI
pre_requisite: Engineering Mathematics-I (TMA101); Engineering Mathematics-II (TMA201); Python Programming (TCS346) or Joy of Computing using Python (TCS361)
difficulty_reason: Broad two-part course: AI search (BFS/DFS, A*, hill climbing, simulated annealing) plus data science and statistics (distributions, regression, time series, ANOVA) implemented in Python (Pandas/Seaborn) and R. Moderate maths and tool breadth.
key_background_areas: Probability and calculus (Engineering Mathematics I/II); Python basics; basic statistics
syllabus_topics: Intro to AI, intelligent agents; uninformed and informed search, A*, local search (hill climbing, simulated annealing, beam); data science process, EDA, Pandas, visualization (Seaborn, maps); populations/samples, statistical modelling, probability distributions, model fitting; R basics, descriptive statistics, plots; linear, logistic and exponential regression, time series, ANOVA, correlation and covariance
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/4TH-Sem-Curriculum-and-Syllabus-Jan-2026.pdf

name: Blockchain and its Applications
difficulty_reason: Conceptual NPTEL course with weekly assignments: cryptographic primitives, consensus protocols, and hands-on Ethereum and Hyperledger smart contracts. Little heavy mathematics, but it needs comfort with networks, cryptography ideas and some coding. Rated from the NPTEL course (GEHU lists it only as "Through Swayam"), so treat as an estimate.
key_background_areas: Cryptography basics (hash functions, digital signatures); computer networks; operating system basics; basic programming
syllabus_topics: Introduction to blockchain and its evolution; cryptographic primitives (hash functions, digital signatures); consensus mechanisms in permissioned and permissionless systems; Ethereum (permissionless) and Hyperledger (permissioned) platforms; smart contracts hands-on; decentralized identity management; blockchain interoperability; risks and attacks (e.g. selfish mining); blockchain applications (final week)
syllabus_source: NPTEL/SWAYAM course "Blockchain and its Applications", IIT Kharagpur (Prof. Sandip Chakraborty, Prof. Shamik Sural), 12 weeks: https://nptel.ac.in/courses/106105235 and syllabus PDF https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/syllabus_pdf/106105235.pdf. Assumed to be the course behind GEHU's "TCS 433 (Through Swayam)" entry; the Sem IV elective forms do not name the instructor.

name: Virtualization and Cloud Computing
pre_requisite: Fundamental of Computer & Introduction to Programming (TCS101); Fundamental of Cloud Computing and Big Data (TCS351)
difficulty_reason: Mostly conceptual, but covers virtualization internals (process/system virtual machines, instruction emulation, dynamic binary optimization, Intel VT-x) and parallel/distributed computing models, which are systems-level and abstract. No mathematics or heavy coding.
key_background_areas: Operating systems and computer organization concepts; TCS351 cloud fundamentals
syllabus_topics: Cloud computing introduction and reference model, AWS/Azure/Google AppEngine/Hadoop overview; virtualization taxonomy (full, para, hardware, desktop, storage, network), Xen, VMware, Hyper-V; process and system virtual machines, Intel VT-x case study; parallel vs distributed computing, RPC, distributed object frameworks; cloud architectures (workload distribution, resource pooling, dynamic scalability, bursting), migration to cloud
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/4TH-Sem-Curriculum-and-Syllabus-Jan-2026.pdf

name: Introduction to Big Data
pre_requisite: Introduction to Statistical Data Science (TCS342); Data Structures with C (TCS302)

key_background_areas: Basic statistics (TCS342); data structures; basic database ideas
syllabus_topics: Big data definition, characteristics, BI vs big data; structured vs unstructured data and sources; big data stack layers, security, operational databases, analytical warehouses; NoSQL and NewSQL, PostgreSQL, key-value, document, columnar and graph databases; basic, advanced and operationalized analytics
syllabus_source: http://btechcsegehu.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/4TH-Sem-Curriculum-and-Syllabus-Jan-2026.pdf

name: Foundation of Cyber Security

key_background_areas: Introduction to Cryptography (TCS392); basic programming (Python); basic networking and Linux usage
syllabus_topics: Cyber security concepts, zero trust, CIA triad, hacker types, penetration testing phases; Linux commands, Bash scripting, Python basics; virtualization setup, IPv4/IPv6, TCP 3-way handshake, netcat, ICMP, Wireshark; client-server web model, XSS, phishing, SQL injection, web pentest tools; malware, password attacks, DDoS, ransomware, man-in-the-middle, spoofing, Tor

name: System Design
pre_requisite: Fundamental of Computer & Introduction to Programming (TCS101) or Introduction to Python Programming (TCS102); Object Oriented Programming (TCS307/TCS346/TCS408)
difficulty_reason: Design-heavy rather than math-heavy: clean code, SOLID, design patterns and LLD case studies, then HLD (load balancing, caching, sharding, CAP, messaging, auth) and large system case studies. Needs solid OOP plus database/networking awareness; breadth and open-ended design judgement are the main difficulty.
key_background_areas: Object-oriented programming (C++/Java/Python); data structures; databases and basic networking
syllabus_topics: Clean coding, OOP principles, UML class/sequence and ER diagrams, machine coding; SOLID, creational/behavioral/structural design patterns; LLD case studies (Tic Tac Toe, LRU Cache, Parking Lot, ATM, Elevator, ticket booking); architecture, scaling, latency vs throughput, REST/RPC/GraphQL/WebSockets, load balancing, caching (Redis), ACID vs BASE, CAP theorem, replication, sharding; NoSQL databases, async processing (RabbitMQ, Kafka, Pub/Sub), authentication and authorization (JWT, OAuth2, OpenID Connect, HTTPS); HLD case studies (food delivery, ride sharing, payments, URL shortener, e-commerce, social media, chat)
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 5th-Sem-Syllabus-2024-28-Batch.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Machine Learning
pre_requisite: Python Programming (TCS346) or Joy of Computing using Python (TCS361); familiarity with data handling concepts
difficulty_reason: Applied ML with Python/scikit-learn: statistics refresher, EDA, supervised algorithms (regression, trees, forests, SVM, KNN, Naive Bayes), clustering, PCA, cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning. Library-driven with moderate maths. Note: the Course Outcomes table in the PDF appears copied from a data-structures course and does not match the units; rating is based on the unit contents.
key_background_areas: Python (lists, dicts, file handling, NumPy); basic statistics; some linear algebra and probability helps
syllabus_topics: Statistics review (mean, median, mode, deviation, outliers); ML paradigms (supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement); Python, NumPy, scikit-learn; EDA, data transformation, missing data, Matplotlib/Seaborn; linear and logistic regression, decision trees, random forest, SVM, KNN, CN2, Naive Bayes; K-means, silhouette score, hierarchical, fuzzy c-means, DBSCAN; dimensionality reduction (variance/correlation filters, feature selection, PCA); cross-validation, evaluation metrics, hyperparameter search (manual, random, grid)
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 5th-Sem-Syllabus-2024-28-Batch.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Foundation of Quantum Computing
pre_requisite: Programming for Problem Solving (TCS201); Python Programming (TCS346) or Joy of Computing using Python (TCS361)
difficulty_reason: Abstract and mathematical: Dirac notation, Hilbert spaces, unitary operators, tensor products, density matrices, no-cloning, multi-qubit circuits, quantum algorithms (Deutsch-Jozsa, Simon, Grover, Shor) and error-correcting stabilizer codes. Prerequisites list only programming, so the linear algebra and quantum mechanics are built up quickly.
key_background_areas: Linear algebra (vectors, matrices, complex numbers); probability; basic Python; algorithm analysis
syllabus_topics: History of quantum computation; superposition, entanglement, interference; Dirac notation, postulates of quantum mechanics, qubits, Pauli and Hadamard gates; linear algebra, tensor products, Hilbert spaces, unitary operators, Born rule, density matrices, no-cloning theorem; Bell states, CNOT/SWAP/Toffoli, circuit model, quantum teleportation, superdense coding; Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, Simon, Grover, Shor; decoherence, quantum error correction, Shor and surface codes, NISQ hardware, BB84, VQE, quantum ML
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 5th-Sem-Syllabus-2024-28-Batch.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Parallel Computer Architecture
difficulty_reason: Advanced architecture topics: shared-memory multiprocessors, cache coherence protocols, directory-based case studies (SGI Origin, Sequent NUMA-Q, with correctness arguments) and memory consistency models. Only basic computer organization is a stated prerequisite, but the protocol-level reasoning is abstract and the NPTEL course is aimed at postgraduate-level depth. Only part of the week-wise syllabus (weeks 1, 2, 7, 8, 9) could be verified.
key_background_areas: Computer organization and architecture (pipelining, caches, virtual memory); operating systems basics
syllabus_topics: Introduction to parallel architectures; memory hierarchy (cache and virtual memory); case studies of Origin (architecture, protocol, correctness) and Sequent NUMA-Q (architecture, protocol, correctness); memory consistency models (sequential and relaxed). Weeks 3-6 and 10-12 not seen.
syllabus_source: https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc25_cs54/preview and https://www.classcentral.com/course/swayam-parallel-computer-architecture-269752 (NPTEL 'Parallel Computer Architecture', Prof. Hemangee K. Kapoor, IIT Guwahati). Alternative: GEHU's Jul 2026 Sem V timetable lists 'TCS 586 Parallel Computer Architecture - Through Swayam (ONLINE)' but does not name the instructor; the IIT Guwahati course is an assumed match (an older NPTEL web course by Mainak Chaudhuri, IIT Kanpur, is also postgraduate-level).

name: Security Audit and Compliance-I
difficulty_reason: Largely descriptive: malware and threat types, cyber laws and compliance standards (IT Act, GDPR, HIPAA, ISO 27001, NIST), access control and encryption concepts, database security, auditing and DR planning. Case studies and light tool use; no mathematics or heavy programming.
key_background_areas: Fundamentals of cyber security; basic databases and networking; basic cryptography concepts
syllabus_topics: Malware (viruses, worms, trojans, botnets, ransomware, spyware), social engineering, phishing, spoofing, cyber stalking; security governance, IT Act 2000, IPR, GDPR, HIPAA, SOX, NIST, ISO 27001; authentication, MFA, RBAC, ACLs, encryption at rest and in transit, SSL/TLS, AES, RSA; data lifecycle, database auditing and monitoring, audit trails, backup and disaster recovery; database vulnerability assessment, penetration testing methodology, security scanning tools
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 5th-Sem-Syllabus-2024-28-Batch.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Computer System Security
difficulty_reason: Technically deep security course: buffer/integer overflows, return-to-libc, race conditions, Dirty COW, format string, Shellshock, Heartbleed, program analysis and fuzzing, web attacks, mobile OS security and Meltdown/Spectre side channels. Needs solid C, operating-system and memory-layout knowledge. No heavy mathematics, but exploit mechanics are conceptually demanding.
key_background_areas: C programming and memory layout; operating systems; computer organization; networking; fundamentals of cyber security
syllabus_topics: Control hijacking, buffer and integer overflow, sandboxing, static/concolic/dynamic analysis, fuzzing; Set-UID programs, return-to-libc, race conditions, Dirty COW, format string, Shellshock, Heartbleed, privilege separation, ASLR and stack canaries; web security (XSS, SQL injection, CSRF, session management, HTTPS, CSP); Android vs iOS security, rootkits, repackaging attacks, whole-disk encryption, malware detection; Meltdown, Spectre, access control lists, capabilities, hardware trojans, supply chain and SCADA security, side-channel attacks
syllabus_source: Uploaded GEHU CSE syllabus: 5th-Sem-Syllabus-2024-28-Batch.pdf (headed Graphic Era Hill University, Dept of CSE)

name: Soft Computing
pre_requisite: Machine Learning (TCS509) or Fundamentals of AI & ML (TCS203)
difficulty_reason: Moderate mathematical content: fuzzy sets, relations and inference, defuzzification, genetic algorithms (encoding, selection, crossover, mutation), multi-objective evolutionary optimization and neural network training. Applied and example-driven, with modest programming; an interdisciplinary course open to CSE/ECE/EE/ME students. Rated from the NPTEL IIT Kharagpur course plan, which GEHU's course is assumed to follow.
key_background_areas: Basic discrete mathematics, sets and logic; basic probability and calculus; basic programming; some linear algebra helps for neural networks
syllabus_topics: Introduction to soft computing; fuzzy logic (fuzzy sets, membership functions, operations, relations, propositions, implications, inference); defuzzification techniques and fuzzy logic controllers; solving optimization problems, genetic algorithms (encoding, selection, crossover, mutation); evolutionary computation, multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (non-Pareto and Pareto approaches); artificial neural networks (architecture, training, applications)
syllabus_source: https://archive.nptel.ac.in/content/syllabus_pdf/106105173.pdf and https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc22_cs54/preview (NPTEL 'Introduction to Soft Computing', Prof. Debasis Samanta, IIT Kharagpur, 8 weeks).
